title: Assistance Plan Revision V1 (one stored revision of one plan, read back as its own bytes)
$comment: DL-KB-12. GET /api/projects/{id}/assistance-plans/{aplan}/revisions/{revision} answers this envelope. The readback (.../assistance-plan-readback/v1) can only serve the NEWEST revision's document -- its `revisions` rows carry a digest, a timestamp and an author, and nothing else -- so before this route the stored body of an older revision was unreadable through any route, and a comparison page could only restate hashes or guess the old text. This document is what makes 「新版本不覆盖历史；对比页读的是两份真实修订」 checkable: two calls, two real documents. `document` is the stored JSON served verbatim and bound by $ref to design-lab/schemas/assistance-plan-v1.schema.json -- the same contract the write path validated these bytes against when they were filed -- rather than being restated here, because a second copy of a document shape is how two owners start disagreeing. `revision` is the number that was asked for and `latest_revision` is the plan's highest, so `is_latest` is the pair a reader can check by hand instead of a word the service asserts; `is_chosen` is true only when a named human adopted THIS revision, computed by the same one query the readback's `choice` is built from. `provided` is this revision's own answer to 'does this row carry creative text', mirroring the readback's `_provided`, and `content_sha256` / `created_at` / `created_by` are this row's columns, not the newest row's. Deliberately absent: the plan's four-state block (`saved`/`provided`/`chosen`/`externally_verified`) is the readback's answer and is not copied here -- two envelopes computing the same states is two truths that can drift -- and there is no field at all that could report a run, a send or a delivery, because reading one stored revision neither performs nor proves any of those. `does_not_say` is the plan store's own list, served unchanged.
